text: Raw or undercooked meat, fish and eggs.
Milk that is not pasteurised or well boiled.
Fruits and vegetables that have not been washed well.
Caffeine from tea, coffee, cola and energy drinks. WHO advises lowering your intake if you have more than 300 mg of caffeine a day. Ask your clinician how much is safe for you.
Large predatory fish that can be high in mercury. Ask your clinician which fish to choose.
Herbal mixtures and traditional concoctions. Check with your clinician before taking any.
Vitamin A capsules or extra vitamin A supplements. They are not recommended for pregnant women unless your clinician prescribes them. Choose vitamin A foods instead.
